Requested: Fund Tx3 by TxPipe to deliver an open API layer for Cardano dApp protocols with developer and AI-agent-facing infrastructure over 12 months.
Recipient: TxPipe, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor

Deliverables: Open, standardized interface across Cardano's leading on-chain protocols, Documentation, auto-generated SDKs in multiple languages, and live JSON-RPC endpoints from verified interface definitions, Agent-first documentation, protocol skills packaging operations, and an MCP server for protocol discovery and calls, Twelve additional protocol onboardings, three per quarter, with full developer and agent coverage, Use of Intersect treasury management smart contracts with milestone-based disbursement controls

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal requests 1,308,000 ADA plus a 327,000 ADA contingency reserve over 12 months, with a total withdrawal of 1,684,050 ADA including a 49,050 ADA Intersect administration fee.

Claim (adoption, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The proposal says Cardano currently lacks a common interface mechanism across the ecosystem, forcing integrators to relearn each protocol and rebuild understanding independently.

Claim (technical, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposer claims AI agents will become a major source of on-chain activity and require shared, auditable, deterministic protocol interfaces to reduce risks from hallucinated transactions.

Claim (adoption, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): Through Catalyst Fund 14, TxPipe has already put the developer layer into production with five protocols live on the Tx3 Protocol Registry.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal commits to onboarding twelve additional protocols, three per quarter, with developer and agent coverage, and to developing the MCP server and skill framework as shared registry infrastructure.
